title: RFI Log
oneLiner: Free RFI and submittal log for small general contractors: write an RFI on the phone, send the architect or owner a reply link, keep the log with due dates
customer: Small US general contractors and subcontractors on projects too small for Procore
revenueModel: Free single RFI with PDF; paid tier for a saved project log, reply links, reminders and team use

paidPrice.product: Fieldwire Business Plus at USD 89 a user a month, the first Fieldwire plan with RFIs and submittals (free Basic has neither). About Rs 8,391 at 94.2754 INR per USD

searches.note: seodata.dev (Google Ads monthly averages, United States, cached 26 Aug 2026) for rfi template; submittal log from https://api.seodata.dev/v1/keyword?q=submittal+log&country=us (construction submittal log 390, submittal log template 210 also shown); rfi log from DataForSEO Google Ads search volume (United States) through Firecrawl Alexandria, request 4908d495-cca6-4d96-82d7-3c3039db7ae2, read 2026-11-27. rfi forms 720 and request for information templates 720 are left out because they mix in procurement intent. Risk: rfi template itself also carries some procurement intent.

screen.freeGap: Free RFI help is templates: Smartsheet, Procore and Down to Bid give Word, Excel or PDF RFI forms (https://smartsheet.com/content/construction-rfi-templates, https://procore.com/library/rfi-templates, https://downtobid.com/blog/rfi-template). Fieldwire's free Basic plan has no RFIs (https://www.Fieldwire.Com/pricing/). Gap: a free RFI log with an answer link for the architect and due dates, no account. Risk: Procore, Smartsheet and Archdesk hold page one.

serp.notes: rfi template: 9 of 10 weak - mitti.com RFI log template page, scribd.com x2 static PDF/Word, pinterest.com x3 thin pins, ingenious.build small blog, dailybuild.co small single-purpose site with a free Excel log, planspan.ai small template page; only surveysparrow.com is a mid-size form builder. submittal log: 6 of 10 weak - constructionlogs.com Excel download, ingenious.build blog, submittal.com small site, mylosscontrolservices.com static .xlsx, dailybuild.co blog, permute.ai small blog; strong are projectmanager.com, autodesk.com, fieldwire.com, procore.com. Counted on the weaker of the two terms. No free web tool on page one does the job end to end: dailybuild and mitti give static templates (dailybuild Excel with no reply link, checked https://dailybuild.co/free-construction-rfi-log-template). Caveat: Firecrawl search results are a proxy for Google page one, not Google itself; Procore, Smartsheet and Autodesk still appear for the second term.

evidence.claim: Fieldwire, a construction app with a free Basic plan, keeps RFIs, submittals and change orders for its Business Plus plan at USD 89 a user a month.
Procore publishes free RFI templates as a lead magnet for its paid RFI tool.
Smartsheet ranks with a free collection of construction RFI form templates in Word and Excel.
DailyBuild ranks on page one for rfi template with a free Excel RFI log template (no signup), a static spreadsheet with no reply link for the architect.

A small commercial GC in Los Angeles with about 40 active jobs tracks RFIs and change orders in Google Sheets, calls Procore too heavy, and replies say Procore is pricey (one estimates about USD 20k a year on a USD 15M job) and that smaller GCs look for cheaper alternatives (r/ConstructionManagers thread 1aocj9c, read through a Redlib mirror).

The owner of a small commercial general contractor (under USD 10M) asked for software with a board to track RFIs and hold stakeholders accountable, found Procore more than they needed, and later chose Procore anyway.

A Mike Holt forum member tracking RFIs in a spreadsheet and word processor asked for software made for this purpose; replies point to AIA document software, Oracle Expedition or a home made Access database.
Knowify sells RFI and submittal tracking with response due dates and an approval portal for respondents, starting at USD 99 a month.
A Payhip seller lists an RFI plus Submittal Log Kit (Excel and Google Sheets workbook, PDF forms, guide) at USD 19, with a USD 15 a month membership; the page shows no reviews or sales counts.

nextAction: None. Killed on the business case.

lead.name: Kabeer
lead.trait: Turns a rough idea into a working page by evening.

terms.rfi template: Page one is mostly procurement intent and big brands: safetyculture.com, docs.oracle.com x2, asana.com x2, Harvard PDF, notion.com, Google Docs, spendflo.com, autodesk.com x2, responsive.io, clickup.com, monday.com, mass.gov, smartsheet.com x2, projectmanager.com x2, casrai.org, visme.co, levelset.com (Procore), mastt.com. Construction results are Autodesk, Smartsheet, ProjectManager, Levelset and Mastt. Small weak sites seen on the first source (mitti, dailybuild, planspan, scribd, pinterest) did not appear.
terms.rfi log: Page one is mostly off topic (radio frequency interference, remote file inclusion attacks, NetApp RTFI, Oracle and AGI docs, Wikipedia) plus help pages from Newforma, Autodesk Forma Build, Hexagon EcoSys and a Freshdesk help article. No free RFI log tool ranks.

killReason: CEO no-go on the business case. Score 17 of 35 against a bar of 24: pain 3, willingnessToPay 3, marketSize 2, distribution 2, competitionGap 2, speedToRevenue 2, recurringRevenue 3. Contractors pay for RFI tracking only inside suites (Fieldwire Business Plus, https://fieldwire.com/pricing/business-plus; Knowify from USD 99 a month, https://knowify.com/rfi-submittal-management-software/). The log itself is free from Procore (https://procore.com/library/rfi-templates) and Smartsheet (https://www.smartsheet.com/content/construction-rfi-templates), and the one open edge, a no-account reply link for the architect, already exists in Raken guest mode on its Performance plan (https://help.rakenapp.com/en/articles/14540383-rfis-overview). The 1,530 monthly searches are small and mixed with procurement and radio intent, and page one for rfi template is held by SafetyCulture, Oracle, Asana, Notion, Autodesk, ClickUp, monday, Smartsheet, ProjectManager and Levelset (cases/rfi-log.md sources 11 and 12, rechecked 28 Nov 2026). No sizing was done; the case bar already fails.
